description: Insecure Data Transmission Due to Missing TLS Without TLS encryption, data transmitted between services and to/from the API Gateway travels in plaintext, making it susceptible to interception and manipulation. An attacker with network access could perform man-in-the-middle attacks to intercept sensitive user data, recommendation data, or authentication tokens.
references: recommendation: Implement TLS for all service communications using AWS Certificate Manager (ACM)

description: Insufficient Network Segmentation for Customer Data While the CDK code shows basic network segmentation, there might be overly permissive security group rules or insufficient subnet isolation that could allow unauthorized access to customer data stores. A compromised application component could potentially access customer data stores directly, bypassing intended access patterns and security controls.
references: recommendation: Implement stricter network segmentation and security group rules

description: ML Model Tampering Through Unsafe Serialization Unsafe deserialization of ML models can lead to code execution vulnerabilities if the model format allows arbitrary code execution during loading. An attacker could upload a maliciously crafted model file that, when loaded by the inference service, executes arbitrary code or manipulates the recommendation system's behavior.
references: owaspTop10: A08:2021-Software and Data Integrity Failures
recommendation: Implement secure model serialization and validation

description: Insufficient Access Controls on API Gateway While IAM authentication is implemented, the API caller policy grants broad access to all API methods without fine-grained controls per endpoint or user role. A client with valid IAM credentials could potentially access all API endpoints, including administrative functions, due to overly permissive IAM policies.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1550 - Use Alternate Authentication Material
recommendation: Implement fine-grained API access controls

description: Denial of Service Through Resource Exhaustion While auto-scaling is configured, the system might be vulnerable to application-layer DoS attacks or resource exhaustion through complex queries. An attacker could overwhelm the system by sending many computationally expensive recommendation requests or by exhausting connection pools to backend services.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1498 - Network Denial of Service
